You've traveled through unfamiliar lands and ventured where roads and maps offer little assistance. Whether guiding travelers or charting wilderness, you've learned to read the land and recognize danger.

Raised among wealth and influence, you learned the importance of reputation, social etiquette, and carefully chosen words. Whether born into minor nobility or a prosperous family, your upbringing opened doors for you. What you do with those privileges is up to you.

The dead have always been part of your livelihood. Whether in cemeteries or ancient crypts, years of hard labor taught you endurance and familiarity with burial customs. You've learned that the dead rarely cause as much trouble as the living.

You know the value of a hard day's work. Whether you grew crops, tended livestock, or helped maintain a family holding, your early life was shaped by the rhythms of the land and the changing seasons. You learned to make do with what you had and mend what was broken. The work was rarely easy, but you learned patience and the satisfaction of a job well done.

You spent a substantial amount of your life in the deep wilderness. Perhaps you tended a shrine far from any settlements or studied the natural world in the quiet solitude. Life away from the bustle of civilization has taught you the signs of illness and injury and led to a deeper understanding of the natural world around you.
